title: In-situ TEM Combined with Laser Induced Heating to Initiate Controlled Silicon Nitride Crystallization to Study Reaction Kinetics for Microelectronics Applications
content: Amorphous silicon nitride (a-SiN) is widely used in microelectronics and microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) as a stable insulating film, serving as both a diffusion barrier and structural support in a variety of device architectures [1]. While theoretical models suggest that SiN should resist crystallization up to very high temperatures (∼1300 °C), recent empirical findings have contradicted these assumptions, revealing that ultra-pure thin layers of SiN can crystallize at much lower temperatures [2]. This highlights gaps in our fundamental understanding of the atomic-level mechanisms which govern phase stability, the role of dopants and impurities, and the influence of stress states within these films. This premature crystallization, if uncontrolled, can degrade the insulating properties and introduce crystalline defects like the ones shown in figure 1b below that limit device yield. To help address this challenge, we are conducting a comprehensive investigation into the nucleation and growth mechanisms governing SiN crystallization.
